title: Landing: a serialized queue that merges, with parked collisions resolved through a graph
description:
Owner ruling 2026-09-10, superseding the fast-forward-only landing in bridge plan v9.

WHY the ff-only design was too narrow: it does not degrade under concurrency, it forbids it. Two graphs from the same base H produce A1 and A2 whose parent is H. A1 lands. A2 is then not a descendant of HEAD, so --ff-only refuses - always, with no race and no timing window. Within one phase this never bites (stage 2 is created after stage 1 lands, so its base is already A1); across concurrent phases or workstreams it bites every time.

RULING: land with an ordinary merge. Fast-forward when the branch has not moved, merge commit when it has.

THE PROBLEM THIS OPENS: a merge commit M has a different tree and a different OID than the signed artifact A. The ship gate binds immutable - bdio/gates.py refuses to close unless payload.artifact.commit_oid equals gate.metadata.artifact_ref. So the human signature binds A and does not bind M. Rebase has the same defect and is worse.

PROPOSED RULE (needs a ruling): split on whether a human authored content.
- Clean merge: M has exactly two parents, H and A, and its tree is reproducible by re-running the merge. Provenance is CHECKABLE, so no second signature. The receipt records M, its two parents, and that the merge was clean.
- Conflicted merge: a human authored content nobody approved. That needs its own signature, and only then.

This is narrower than v8, which demanded a signing ceremony for every landing.

CONSEQUENCE: pre-landing verification becomes MORE important, not less. M may be a tree no one has ever tested. The repo gate must run on M in a detached scratch worktree before the real branch moves. supervisor/verify.py:137 VerifyTree is close but not identical - it asserts head == commit on a plain checkout, and this needs a checkout of H that a merge is then performed in.

STAYS CUT from v8: the CAS, the band lock across admission and landing, the conflict fixture and interloper, the OID-bound resolution gate with its nine-field payload, and the blanket per-landing ceremony.
acceptance_criteria: A landing whose branch has not moved fast-forwards to the signed OID. A landing whose branch has moved produces a merge commit, verifies the repo gate on that merge commit in a detached tree before the branch moves, and records both parents in the receipt. A conflicted merge refuses and reports; it never auto-resolves. A ruling is recorded on what authorizes a merge commit the signature does not cover.
notes:
Owner rulings 2026-09-10, in conversation:

1. LAND BY MERGE, not ff-only. Fast-forward when the branch has not moved, merge commit when it has. ff-only does not degrade under concurrency, it FORBIDS it: two graphs from base H produce artifacts whose parent is H, the first lands, and every later one is not a descendant of HEAD so --ff-only always refuses.

2. SERIALIZE LANDING, NOT WORK. The graph run is the expensive part (36-55 min, $2-4) and stays parallel. The repo gate is cheap (measured ~4 min this session: 76s + 22s + 105s + 19s + checks) and serializes behind a landing lock. Ten stages: ~400 min fully serial, ~80 min with parallel graphs and a serial landing queue, ~50 min if clean merges are batched into one gate run.

3. PARKED, NOT ABANDONED. A stuck landing never blocks the queue and never discards the work. Re-running a stage is for work that is genuinely invalidated, NOT a collision policy - a policy of abandon-on-collision makes concurrency cost more than working serially, which is self-defeating.

4. THREE LANDING PATHS. (a) HEAD unmoved: fast-forward, repo gate on A, land. (b) HEAD moved, clean merge: repo gate on M - M is a tree nobody has tested. Green lands with NO new signature, because M has exactly two parents and its tree is reproducible by re-running the merge, so provenance is checkable. (c) HEAD moved, conflict OR clean-merge-with-red-gate: park and resolve through a graph. The red-gate case is the one a conflict check misses - B renames a function, A calls the old name, different files, git merges cleanly, code is broken.

5. VERIFY BEFORE THE BRANCH MOVES. Mandatory now rather than merely cheaper: M may be a tree neither the implementer, the reviewer, nor the signer ever saw.

STILL CUT from v8: the CAS (a landing lock makes compare-and-swap unnecessary - one writer), the band lock across admission AND landing (the lock is scoped to landing only), the conflict fixture and interloper commit, the OID-bound resolution gate with its nine-field payload, and the per-landing signing ceremony.

title: Decide what an orchestrator signature MEANS, and which gates may take one
description: Today a signature is a person accepting responsibility for an immutable OID. An LLM signature is a different claim and the graph should be able to say which gates accept it. Likely shape: a per-gate declaration of permitted signer classes, so ship stays human-only while triage or a future low-risk gate may be orchestrator-closable. This is the ruling the other two tasks depend on - do it first.
acceptance_criteria: A written ruling recorded in the ADR set or the spec; the graph schema can express per-gate permitted signer classes; a graph declaring an impossible combination is refused at load.
notes: Superseded by the owner-approved 2026-09-11 coordination spec and cr-bwo.4. Preserve attributable model decisions and explicit escalation, but implement them through ordinary task execution and durable decision records, not model signing keys or human gate closure. Human-only signed gates remain unchanged. This is a contract supersession, not a claim that the original proposed signing mechanisms were implemented.

title: Add a second signing principal so an orchestrator signature is attributable
description: Mechanically the allow-list is a file (scripts/make-foreman-config.sh:33-35 makes signers_dir, gate_key, allowed_signers). Adding a second principal is trivial. The design work is making the CLOSED-GATE RECORD say which principal signed, so "a human approved this" stays a checkable fact and does not silently become "something approved this".
acceptance_criteria: A closed gate records the signing principal; a test asserts a human-signed and an orchestrator-signed approval are distinguishable after the fact.

title: Add an escalate outcome so the orchestrator can decline to decide
description: Without it, "I should not be the one deciding this" has no legal move and becomes a stall. Escalate must be a first-class outcome that leaves the gate open for a human principal, not a refusal and not an abandon.
acceptance_criteria: An orchestrator can close its turn with escalate; the gate stays open for a human signature; the escalation and its reason are recorded and visible in foreman status.

title: create_root validates the pinned body only AFTER writing it — move validation before _create_bead
description:
Discovered while fixing cr-xb2 round 6, by observing what the RED test actually printed.

create_root ALREADY enforces the graph schema. It does so too late. The post-write path _converged_root -> _ensure_self_id -> parse_root -> load_pinned_body re-validates the pinned body against graph_schema.json. Observed directly: a task node with runner="claude" logs wf.root.created root_id=wf-1 and THEN raises PinnedGraphMismatchError with "schema at $.node[0].runner: claude does not match ^profile:[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*$".

So a schema-invalid programmatic body is not silently accepted. It is WRITTEN, then rejected -- leaving the caller an exception plus a permanently poisoned instance key, because root identity refuses to recreate that key with a corrected body. The invariant exists; only its ordering is wrong.

FIX DIRECTION, and note it is NOT a ^profile: regex. Call load_pinned_body(canonical_bytes(definition.document), allow_test_flags=allow_test_flags) up beside the other _assert_ guards, before _create_bead. That makes create-time and load-time agree by construction and closes EVERY schema drift at once, not just runner -- any programmatic model_copy producing a body the reader will later refuse. A hand-written pattern check at this boundary would be a second narrower copy of a rule the schema already owns, and it would drift.

The boundary is correct: create_root is already the documented chokepoint for _assert_tasks_are_instructed, precisely because there is no CLI instantiate command and labs call it directly. The programmatic path is the one the TOML loader never covers.

WHAT IT BREAKS, checked: three regressions in tests/test_bdio_seams_roots.py build a literal runner incidentally while testing a MISSING RESOLVED-CONFIG PIN. Each would start failing on the runner-pattern message instead of its intended message. Each retargets by keeping runner="profile:implementer" and stripping only the config pin. One test name becomes a misnomer and should be renamed. Nothing else found: instructions is not schema-required (required is name and kind only; ADR 0002 enforces it at create_root instead), so the two instructions regressions are unaffected.

COST: one canonical-serialize plus jsonschema validate per new-key create. Bounded, paid once per instance, and the same work already happens on the read side.

JUDGEMENT CALL to settle when actioning: this makes create_root reject bodies that GraphDefinition construction accepted, so the Pydantic model stays looser than the carrier. That is already true today via the post-write read; the change only makes it honest and non-destructive.

This is the third time this boundary surfaced today from unrelated directions -- the disciplines review (where a claim checker belongs), the cr-xb2 model-pin guard, and this. create_root is the real boundary and the validator is one layer too high.
close_reason: Merged 865b598. Root creation now validates and pins the body before writing: canonical bytes are re-validated through load_pinned_body, the declared hash is compared, and runner/model/effort are required for every task. Prevents a root whose every later read raises at parse_root. Reviewed Terra -> Opus 5 medium -> Sol high (SHIP). Merged-result gates all seven green: 1288 not-bd-not-live, 123 proc, 22 bd, 66 acceptance, ruff check+format clean, mypy --strict clean on 91 files.

title: A steer that crashes between close_activation and mint strands the instance forever
description:
Found by GPT-5.6 Sol on the cr-xb2 round 4 review. Distinct from cr-xb2: this is a recovery-lifecycle defect, not root-pin divergence, and the crash half is pre-existing.

Steerer.resume closes the parent (supervisor/steer.py:226) BEFORE the root read, the two pin reads, and the mint at :238-254. Anything that fails in that window -- a crash, a bd read failure, or pinned_execution_setting raising for a legacy root with no pins -- leaves a closed steered activation with no continuation.

Recovery cannot repair it. classify() discards the intent for closed lifecycles (supervisor/recover.py:229), so on re-entry route_head invokes recovery, receives no action, and returns no progress (foreman/cases.py:408). Ordinary ticks then repeat forever with no forward motion and no operator signal beyond the stall.

The resume docstring claims every step is idempotent so recovery can re-enter at an unknown crash point. That claim is FALSE for the close-to-mint window specifically. The close-forward repair it describes works for already-settled rows; it does not cover a settled row whose continuation was never minted.

Fix direction from Sol: make a closed steered head that still has a persisted intent re-enter the idempotent continuation mint when no continuation exists. Normalize the intent before the destructive work while retaining close-forward repair for already-settled rows.

Note the interaction with cr-xb2 round 5: once the creation guard covers every execution setting, the legacy-root trigger narrows to roots created before that guard. The crash trigger is unaffected and is the durable half of this bug.
close_reason: Merged 64e62b7. A fresh steer no longer destroys a running child for a refusal knowable beforehand: the race plan and supersede_activation now share _may_be_superseded, and the mint preflight shares the whole non-writing preparation. Four rounds (pins -> bounds -> race -> race predicate); each round found the prior fix modelled a subset of the real path. Residual is honest and structural: TOCTOU cannot be closed by a preflight. Reviewed Terra -> Opus 5 medium -> Sol high (SHIP, no findings). Merged-result gates all seven green.

title: Record which rules are load-bearing for build-loop's TDD, with enforcement tier per rule
description:
The v1-scoped half of the disciplines work. The discipline FRAMEWORK (library, claim checker, composition) is out of v1; this doc is what carries its value at near-zero cost.

build-loop enforces TDD through four mechanisms of descending strength, and nothing in the repo says which rule rests on which:

1. tick / topology -- ordering (write_tests before review_tests before implement)
2. bwrap mounts -- write scope via allowed_paths
3. pinned verifiers -- tests-untouched.sh, assertion-strength.sh, mutate.sh
4. prose -- node instructions, e.g. "each test must be able to fail"

The concrete risk this closes is already half-realised. implement allowed_paths was widened from tests/unit/** to tests/** for cr-o85.34.21, so the entire do-not-edit-your-own-yardstick rule migrated from a sandbox guarantee (tier 2) to a single verifier (tier 3). The comment at workflows/build-loop.toml:110-116 states this, but nothing declares that verifier load-bearing for a discipline. Delete it and the graph still validates, the hash moves, and TDD is silently prose-only.

Deliverable: a doc listing each rule that constitutes build-loop TDD, its tier, and the file:line that enforces it. It is also the artifact a future claim checker consumes, so keep it structured.

Related: cr-5fs (the recovery path that bypasses tier 1 entirely).
close_reason: Merged to main and re-verified on the merged result (1278 / 119 proc / 22 bd / 59 acceptance passed, ruff + mypy clean). cr-xb2: six rounds, merge 8c16835. cr-5fs + cr-by6: merge in the disciplines branch.

title: build-loop: every tests-region node's infra-retry fallback lands in triage_build, whose rebudget enters implement
description:
Traced in source, not reproduced live.

The tests region is bounded by on_exhausted = triage_tests, whose rebudget edge correctly returns to write_tests. That covers REGION_ROUNDS exhaustion only.

INFRA_RETRIES exhaustion takes a different route. foreman/bounds.py refusal_route uses node.fallback or index.document.fallback. review_tests declares no node-level fallback, so it falls through to the document fallback, which build-loop.toml sets to triage_build. foreman/cases.py then opens a transition gate on that node. triage_build outcomes are only rebudget and abandon, and its rebudget edge targets implement.

Result: if review_tests exhausts infrastructure retries, the only non-abandon option available to the human jumps straight to implement, having never obtained review_tests.accept. The test-first ordering that the graph otherwise enforces topologically is bypassed on this path.

It is not silent -- a human must open the gate. But the gate is named triage_build and its rebudget outcome reads as give the build more budget, not waive test review. The recovery vocabulary cannot express the correct action, which is resume test review.

Options: give review_tests a node-level fallback pointing at triage_tests; or widen the triage outcome set so a human can route back to the test region; or make the document fallback region-aware.

Found by GPT-6 Astra during the disciplines review and confirmed independently against bounds.py, cases.py and build-loop.toml.
notes:
SCOPE CORRECTION (Claude Fable 5.1, confirmed independently): this is a CLASS, not one node. Verified: the string fallback occurs exactly once in workflows/build-loop.toml -- the document-level [fallback] table. No node declares a node-level fallback. Since bounds.py refusal_route uses node.fallback or index.document.fallback for INFRA_RETRIES, EVERY tests-region task node (write_tests and review_tests) routes to triage_build on infra-retry exhaustion, and triage_build rebudget enters implement.

Astra traced it via review_tests; Fable traced it via write_tests. Same class, two instances.

Fix accordingly: a node-level fallback on every tests-region node pointing at triage_tests, not a patch to one node. Alternative framing worth considering: make the document fallback region-aware so the default is structurally correct rather than restated per node.
close_reason: Merged to main and re-verified on the merged result (1278 / 119 proc / 22 bd / 59 acceptance passed, ruff + mypy clean). cr-xb2: six rounds, merge 8c16835. cr-5fs + cr-by6: merge in the disciplines branch.

title: execution skill: the all-stages-closed discipline gate is unsatisfiable
description:
Found by an Opus 5 review of the bridge plan on 2026-09-07 and confirmed by measurement. .claude/skills/execution/SKILL.md:89-96 gates a phase close on: n=$(bd list --parent <epic> --json | jq length); u=$(unclosed count); [ "$n" -gt 0 ] && [ "$u" -eq 0 ]. But bd list --parent omits closed children unless --all is passed. Measured on the closed epic cr-o85.33: without --all it returns 0 rows, with --all it returns 12. So at the exact moment every child is closed, n becomes 0 and the gate fails its own n>0 precondition. The gate can never pass. This is independent of the bridge work; any phase closed through this skill either never hit the gate or it was overridden.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Take an epic whose children are all closed, e.g. cr-o85.33.
2. Run: bd list --parent cr-o85.33 --json | jq length  -> 0
3. Run: bd list --parent cr-o85.33 --all --json | jq length  -> 12
4. Substitute into the SKILL.md:89-96 gate: n=0, so [ "$n" -gt 0 ] is false and the phase cannot close.
acceptance_criteria: The gate counts closed children (--all or equivalent) so that a fully-closed epic passes and an epic with any unclosed child fails; a test or a worked example pins both directions.
close_reason: Fixed in 88bbb17. All three bd list --parent invocations in the phase-close gate now pass --all, with the reason stated inline so it is not simplified back out. Verified by running the corrected gate verbatim: cr-o85.33 (fully closed) n=12 u=0 PASS; cr-o85.34 (partial) n=30 u=5 FAIL naming all five. references/workstream-mode.md:76 checked and unaffected — an explicit --status filter overrides the default.

title: Discipline composition: Node has no method or discipline-set field, so mount-many has no mechanism
description: GPT-6 Astra audit 2026-09-07, confirmed. schema/models.py:222 gives Node instructions and verify commands but no skill, method or discipline-set field. docs/ideas/workflow-graphs.md:50 made mount many, not route one an agreed design constraint: TDD plus incremental plus source-verification should compose onto one task. build-loop encodes ONE test-first shape by hand instead. cr-b1p and ADR 0003 cover only the storage half (resolve-copy-freeze of a shared method library); how several discipline pointers COMPOSE onto a node is unspecified and unbuilt.
design: Depends on cr-b1p landing the method library first. Then decide composition semantics: ordering, same-key conflict behaviour, and whether a discipline can add verify commands or only instructions. A single reusable instruction reference does not satisfy mount-many on its own.
acceptance_criteria: A node names two or more disciplines and the composed brief contains both, in a defined order, with conflicts resolved by a stated rule; a test pins the composition; build-loop test-first is expressed as a mounted discipline rather than hand-written instructions.

title: Reconcile the spec, plans and tracker with the code that actually shipped
description: GPT-6 Astra audit 2026-09-07. The spec body is stale in ways that made two independent audits start from wrong numbers. docs/specs/workflow-interpreter.md:74 and :508 still describe a MODEL foreman taking manual ticks; ADR 0004 superseded that with deterministic routing, and foreman/__main__.py:494 is a resident poll loop with poll_s/max_wall_s that auto-advances to a gate or stall. title: Durable acceptance matrix: map each of the 28 spec drills to its test and its execution evidence
description: GPT-6 Astra audit 2026-09-07. Only 15 of the 28 spec section 13 drills carry a drill_N name in a test function; the rest are covered under descriptive names, so a grep understates coverage badly. But the opposite claim is also unsupported: no artifact maps drill to test to fresh execution evidence. Astra traced all 28 to assertions and found real coverage everywhere, while noting that some drills use scripted children and reconstructed lab objects rather than killing real vendor processes. Nobody can currently answer which drills are proven end to end.
design: One table, checked in. Per drill: spec line, the test that asserts its postcondition, and the strongest evidence class achieved. Distinguish four classes explicitly: synthetic race residue, lab rebuild, real process crash, real vendor run. Rerun the full gate on a bwrap-capable host and archive sanitized evidence somewhere durable, not scratchpad.

title: token_budget and trim_priority are declared and validated but never consumed — prompts are unbounded
description:
GPT-6 Astra audit 2026-09-07, confirmed by orchestrator. schema/models.py:269 declares source trim_priority and rules_references.py:219 validates it is >= 1, but NO runtime consumer reads it. node.token_budget is threaded to TaskSpec (foreman/supervise.py:171) and profile.py:145 but nothing trims against it. inputs.py materializes every bound input whole: writing outputs become full diffs, non-writing outputs concatenate all output-tree files. A large diff or findings set therefore produces an unexpectedly large prompt with no ceiling. The graph calls token_budget a context-trim budget; today it is decoration.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Author a node with token_budget set and two sources at different trim_priority.
2. Run it where the bound inputs (a large diff, or an output tree with many files) exceed that budget.
3. Inspect the composed brief: every source is present whole, nothing was dropped or truncated.
4. Confirm statically: grep -rn trim_priority workflow_interpreter/ --include=*.py returns only the declaration (schema/models.py:269) and the validation rule (schema/rules_references.py:219). No consumer.
design: Decide first whether trim_priority is the mechanism or should be deleted. If kept, the composer drops or truncates lowest-priority sources until the brief fits token_budget, and records what it dropped in the activation so the trace shows it. Distinct from cr-o85.9, which is about tokens-vs-USD mapping, not prompt composition.
acceptance_criteria: A node with a token_budget and inputs exceeding it produces a brief within budget; the dropped or truncated sources are recorded on the activation; a test pins both the fit and the record. Or: trim_priority is deleted and the validation rule with it.
notes: Superseded by the owner-approved P2 UTF-8 context_budget_bytes contract: whole essential inputs, priority-based optional omission, actual envelope accounting and explicit legacy token_budget diagnostics. This is not exact token accounting; see P2 verification and cr-bwo.4.

title: [P1] Complete sequential execution
description: THE central vision gap, found independently by two audits (2026-09-07 Fable 5.1 + GPT-6 Astra). The engine sits BESIDE the harness workflow instead of under it: .claude/skills/execution/SKILL.md still selects, claims, executes and closes stages in prose, while both graphs start at implement/write_tests. docs/ideas/workflow-graphs.md:24 named replacing that prose as the whole point of the idea. Until one real multi-stage phase runs through wf create + wf run from the normal entry point, the interpreter is a parallel system nobody uses.
design: docs/specs/2026-09-11-workflow-coordination.md
acceptance_criteria: One real multi-stage roadmap phase completes through the interpreter, entered from /phase-execution, with no prose stage loop running in parallel; stage closure and gate rendering come from the graph; the run is reproducible from bd + git + the wrapper dir.
notes:
2026-09-07: plan v8 landed, docs/plans/phase-execution-interpreter-bridge.md, 488 lines. Eight Terra rounds, five review passes (Opus 5 medium x3, GPT-5.6 Sol high x2, GPT-6 Astra medium x1).

2026-09-09 MINIMALITY PASS — v8 superseded. All five prior reviews were adversarial CORRECTNESS reviews, which only ever add mechanism; none asked whether a mechanism was necessary. Fable 5.1 high asked that question and returned RESTRUCTURE; GPT-6 Astra high adversarially reviewed the rulings and returned ACCEPT WITH EXCEPTIONS (3). Reports in scratchpad/bridge-min/ (gitignored).

Core finding: the v8 landing core existed to make a TRUE MERGE safe against parallel landings. This repo is single-owner, single-machine, no CI, no other writers. Astra: confidence HIGH that concurrent merge/resolution machinery is unnecessary for criterion 1.

OWNER APPROVED 2026-09-09 — three ruling changes: (1) cut O1 cryptographic re-verification and ref re-dereference; (2) cut Stage 3, the conflict fixture, the interloper commit, the D11 resolution ceremony and the D10 counterfactual — the proof is TWO stages; (3) merge stage bead and source bead into ONE record. Also: keep the proof roadmap, no cleanup commit.

Three MANDATORY Astra corrections in v9: (C1) a full-gate receipt bound to the tested OID must be persisted BEFORE either close — a crash between merge and the first gate command would otherwise close both records with no verification at all; (C2) find_roots is lookup not repair — two concrete crash windows need a real repair path plus fault injection; (C3) --ff-only success does not prove artifact identity — an already-ancestor commit succeeds WITHOUT moving HEAD, so landing must classify fresh / replay / refuse.

Transport finding both models confirmed and five prior reviews missed: GitSubcommand excludes merge (supervisor/gitcmd.py:99-140). Neither v8 nor the ff-only replacement works through the unchanged transport. Resolution: a narrow bridge-local subprocess, bounded, preserving the transport timeouts and config hardening.

Stale in v8: the cr-dbk dependency (fixed 88bbb17 on 2026-09-08); D8 six dead-end kinds (now seven); two of three named source-bead candidates fail O2 eligibility.

Cost falls from 1.8-3.1 graph hours / $6-13 / three ceremonies to roughly 1.2 graph hours / $4-5 / two ceremonies, MINUS whatever the three corrections add back. Treat as a floor.
2026-09-11 owner approved the six-phase roadmap and resuming the paused worktree. Existing bridge defects remain in scope. Fable 5.1 high reviews after P1, P3, P5. No commits/main merge/push. Resume with execution and test-driven-development.
close_reason: All 8 direct children closed; approved P1 exit demonstrated. Full seven gates passed on source digest snapshot; Fable 5.1 high accepted correction; normal phase-bridge completed two real-runtime sequential stages with authenticated fixture-only ship gates and clean verified landing. title: toolchain_env sets UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT but not UV_CACHE_DIR — a bounded node still writes ~/.cache/uv
description: Found while fixing cr-o85.34.22: profiles/_base.py::toolchain_env redirects the project venv into the activation scratch dir but leaves UV_CACHE_DIR at its default, so a bounded node (and any nested vendor sandbox with a read-only HOME) writes or fails on ~/.cache/uv. Then reconsider whether the nested_sandbox marker on that test can be dropped.

title: resolve() accepts a writes=false override on a node with non-empty authored allowed_paths, which graph validation rejects
description: Found by the Opus critic on the 2026-09-05 assessment branch (pre-existing, not introduced). Now that mint._derive_base_commit reads the pinned write mode, the effective node should pass the same semantic rules as the authored graph: run allowed_paths_well_formed (or the full per-node rule set) over the resolved node in _refuse_unusable, and fix the test that constructs the invalid combination.

title: phase-5: test_steer_proc_raises_its_own_flag_and_kills_a_genuinely_live_child is load-sensitive — 2 failures in ~8 full-suite runs
description:
Observed 2026-09-02: the proc-marked steer test failed twice during the
cr-mub/cr-0zc work and passed on every other run — 3 consecutive clean
full-suite runs (984 passed) immediately after, plus 2 clean `-m proc` runs and
a clean single-test run, with no code change in between.

Both failures happened while other work was competing for the machine (the live
DRILL-27 rig had detached wrapper processes running). The test forks a REAL
child and asserts it is alive within a timing window, so scheduler pressure is
the obvious suspect.

Not diagnosed: the failure output was swallowed by the `-q` summary and the
test passed on every attempt to reproduce it, so there is no traceback. Do NOT
"fix" this by widening the window blind — the liveness assertion's PLACEMENT is
load-bearing (a mutation probe earlier in the same session showed the
assertion is dead if it sits after `await_barrier`, recorded in
.claude/project/learnings.md). Capture a real traceback first, under
`--tb=long` with the machine loaded.

Reproduction attempt: run the full suite with the live rig ticking in parallel.
notes:
2026-09-04 FIRST REAL TRACEBACK (phase-6 E2 live run, verify log /tmp/verify-feature.4079170.log, also failed 07:19 in review r1 of root wf-y6q and once in review r2 of wf-rjq):
  steer.py:202 steer -> steer.py:224 resume -> store.close_activation(STEERED) -> transitions.py:125
  LifecycleConflictError: activation wf-3 already recorded outcome error_transport at lifecycle closed
Sequence in the log: 07:18:29 child launched + stale flag mirrored; 07:18:30 wf.steer.session_pinned; then the conflict. So steer() ran within 1s of launch and lost a race: between its terminate() and its close_activation(STEERED), the forked WRAPPER's own monitor cycle observed the child dead and closed the activation as exit_unobserved -> error_transport (run.py _exit_reason fallthrough; monitor.py _unreapable_reason returns None when reaped.ours and no code). The wrapper never reads steer_intent (grep run.py/exit.py/monitor.py: no reader), so the intent written before the kill cannot make it defer; only foreman-side recovery (recover._case) honours STEER_PENDING. Under load the wrapper's cycle lands inside steer's kill->close window more often. This is a product race, not a timing-window test bug: the activation ends error_transport with a steer intent on disk, and the next tick's recovery finishes the steer. Fix candidates: (1) the wrapper's exit path checks steer_intent before grading and records ExitReason steered / defers the close; (2) steer() holds the wrapper's activation lock (wrapper.lock exists) across kill->close. Do NOT widen the test's window. Live consequence: this test sits in scripts/verify-feature.sh, so a flake at a review node is a fail_code rework round (cr-o85.34.13).
close_reason: Product race fixed: Supervisor._supervise reads steer-intent.json after monitor.watch and, if present, returns without observing the exit (no exit file, no record_exit, no close); the steerer or §5.6 STEER_PENDING recovery owns the close. Second cause found: the test's _runner_alive used bare /proc existence and saw the un-reaped zombie (~3% under load, identical before/after the wrapper fix); it now reads /proc/<pid>/stat and treats state Z as dead, placement unchanged. 30/30 loaded runs green. Gates 1054/70 tests, ruff, format, mypy green.

title: phase-4 DEFECT: snapshot_commit's 'git add --all' honours a runner-writable .gitattributes ⇒ repo-configured clean filters run as the wrapper over runner content (gitio.py:26-35 documented residual)
description: Surfaced by phase-5 planning (Sol r16 N1 on pin_outputs, fixed there with filter-free plumbing: hash-object --no-filters + update-index --cacheinfo). Mitigation shape: enumerate (ls-files -z --others --modified --exclude-standard + deleted) then hash-object --no-filters + update-index --cacheinfo, or GIT_ATTR overrides where possible. Decision pending (user): fold into phase 5 as R8 or keep as a bead.

GitSubcommand.ADD greps to 0. Proven by test_a_runner_gitattributes_cannot_run_a_clean_filter, which plants a real filter.runner.clean and asserts the sentinel was never written and the runner's own bytes survived. title: Guard hook's token check misses heredocs, ANSI-C quoting and quoted substitutions
description:
Found by critic-70f (2026-11-13, scratchpad/mvp-stack/critic-70f.md, "Pre-existing limits" 1 and 2) while reviewing the cr-oez0 fix. Both also hold on the committed hook (HEAD 0 / new 0), so they are not regressions of that fix.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. A Bash command that is valid shell but that Python shlex rejects (a heredoc holding an unmatched quote, or ANSI-C quoting $'...') and that contains a blocked git form behind a global option: the guard's token check exits 3, only the substring check runs, and the command is allowed.
2. A blocked git form reached through a quoted executable spelling or a command substitution inside quotes: the token check does not see it.

## Expected
Policy decided by the owner: either the guard understands these shell forms, or it fails closed when it cannot parse valid shell text.
acceptance_criteria: Each listed shell form with a blocked git command is blocked, or the owner records the limit as accepted; tests cover the decision.

comments.author: cc:940ec94d
comments.text: 2026-11-13: also a comment ending in a backslash: bash does not continue a comment line, but the hook's line-joining merges the next line into the comment, so a blocked git command on that next line is allowed (pre-existing at HEAD; round 4 of cr-oez0, scratchpad/mvp-stack/70/build-report.md).

comments.author: cc:940ec94d
comments.text: 2026-11-13 critic-70h: a carriage return before '#' (': \r#...; git -C /x reset --hard HEAD') makes the token check read a comment where bash does not (shlex treats \r as whitespace); HEAD allowed it too. Evidence: scratchpad/mvp-stack/critic-70h.md.

title: discovery: a source for saved computations, and four more unclear points from the cr-onr1 trials
description:
Found by the three cr-onr1 trial runs (scratchpad/mvp-stack/52/discovery-trial{,2,3}.md) and Sol's reviews (scratchpad/mvp-stack/critic-52e.md, critic-52g.md).

Main gap: a record has no source kind for a computation over the repository (a script counting ledger events, a join, a search). Sessions cited a code line that cannot show the count and graded such rows high, or put counts in a prototype report. Sol (critic-52g R1, R2) found trial 3 still had high rows whose cited line establishes only part of the answer, and one row comparing two different populations (207 report rejects vs 206 revisit_when text matches). Candidate: a `computed: <script path> -> <output path>` source, or requiring such answers to go through prototype. Needs a checker change, so it is a design choice.

Four more unclear points (none of cr-onr1's four):
1. Area when the question's code spans two top-level directories (curation/ and harness_lifecycle/).
2. What a prototype report must contain when it is a record's source (prototype/SKILL.md:27-30 names outcome, cases, limits, pointer).
3. A row that follows from a proposed row: an observed conditional consequence can be established while its prerequisite choice stays proposed (critic-52e).
4. Discovery writes no Beads: where a factual correction to a bead goes (trial 1 found cr-5v7n's count is 33, not 11).
acceptance_criteria: discovery's record can cite a saved computation (a counting script and its output) as evidence, and the skill answers the four points below; a fresh run on a real question with counted facts cites and grades them per SKILL.md's confidence rule, judged row by row by a critic; check_record.py tests pass.
notes:
2026-11-12: build committed d978913 (computed: source + four points; round 2026-11-12-discovery-computed sealed); fresh clone: check ok, 590 passed. Acceptance NOT met: Sol critic-57c (scratchpad/mvp-stack/critic-57c.md) REVISE on both cr-bes trials - assembled answers still graded high (F1), 211 stored events vs 207 actually evaluated (F2), missed existing gap tests (F3), round evidence omits trial records (F4, goes in the next round). Next: a mechanical check in check_record.py - a high row's answer may cite no location but its Source (would have flagged 6 of the 8 rejected rows), plus one more trial; resume with: plan 57 rev / new plan 58.
2026-11-12 ACCEPTANCE NOT MET (trial 3, plan 58 §7): Sol critic-58d FAIL (scratchpad/mvp-stack/critic-58d.md). The new advisory note worked: it fired on rows 2-3 and the session regraded both to medium (both then PASS). Still failing: row 1 and row 5 high on assembled/absence-based evidence (5: zero-unknown inferred from an absent section); Outcome certifies all 211 though gap evaluates 207; row 7 says no test covers the SHA-only baseline but test_scan_tree_hash.py:242-284 does. Per plan 58 trials stop here; the bead stays open and unclaimed for the owner's decision. The checker note commits separately once its build review passes.
close_reason: Closed by owner decision 2026-11-12 with the limit recorded: built d978913 + 494fc75 (computed source, four clarifications, advisory high-grade note); row-by-row acceptance not met in three trials (critic-57c, critic-58d) on research-quality errors no rule can catch. See comment.

comments.text: Owner decision 2026-11-12: accept the limit and close. Delivered: computed: source (d978913), the four clarifications, the advisory high-grade note (494fc75). Acceptance (a fresh run graded row by row) not met in three trials: the note works (trial 3 regraded both noted rows), but population mix-ups (211 stored vs 207 evaluated) and missed existing tests are research quality no grading rule can catch (critic-57c, critic-58d).

title: discovery: clarify four points the first real run found unclear
description:
The D5 end-to-end run (2026-11-11, record scratchpad/mvp-stack/37/discovery-e2e.md, 7 rows, 0 problems) followed discovery on bead cr-7c6i and reported four points the skill leaves unclear:
1. The record's `**Caller:**` field has no defined format.
2. The `**Area:**` rule covers only docs/discovery paths; a caller-named path outside it (the run chose `general`) is not covered.
3. Whether an earlier precedent the owner never confirmed counts as a prior decision to carry forward, or stays `proposed` (the run chose `proposed`).
4. Whether `established` covers an answer derived from several code constraints rather than one cited line.
acceptance_criteria: discovery's SKILL.md or template answers each of the four points below, a fresh run on a real question no longer reports them unclear, and check_record.py still passes its tests.
close_reason: fadbc19 (local, unpushed), plan scratchpad/mvp-stack/52/plan.md. discovery SKILL.md and templates/record.md answer all four points: Caller format; Area/Topic describe the question wherever the file lives; prior decisions need owner authority, unconfirmed precedent is evidence (row stays proposed); confidence high only when the cited source shows the answer by itself, combined/empty-search answers medium or low naming the rest, facts and choices in separate rows. Fresh trial 3 (scratchpad/mvp-stack/52/discovery-trial3.md) reported none of the four unclear; check_record tests pass (584 passed on fresh clone; registry check ok 37 rounds; catalog ok). Limit: Sol (critic-52g) accepts the text but found trial 3 still graded two combined answers high and compared two populations wrongly; the plan's stricter per-case demonstration is not met. Root gap (no source kind for a saved computation) and four new unclear points: cr-oiyn. Rounds 2026-11-12-discovery-clarify, -options, -grading sealed.

title: Scanner: mirror-only and tree-only changes do not show in gap or drift
description:
Inherited limits of the shared scanner, now also on the new playbook kind. No current pstack ruling is affected: its Claude Code copy has a distinct namespace and stays a separate entry, and no playbook has a reference folder at the pin. From critic-2b findings 3 and 4.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Mirror a playbook under .cursor/skills/router/playbooks/a.md, identical to the canonical copy, and rule it. Edit the mirror's body or its reference file: gap reports no gaps. Only the canonical copy's tree hash survives collapse (curation/scan/catalog.py, curation/registry/changes.py).
2. Edit only playbooks/a/ref.md: gap detects it through tree_hash, but scan diff_catalogs returns no material or minor change (curation/scan/drift.py), the same as skill assets today.
3. gap's printed diagnostic diffs only a.md, so it omits the reference that changed (curation/registry/changes.py).
acceptance_criteria: A ruled capability whose mirror copy or reference file changes is reported by gap, or the limit is stated in the registry README with its revisit condition; catalog diff classifies a tree-only change; gap's diagnostic includes a playbook's reference folder.

title: Durable monitor/wake in the foreman: heartbeat-driven wake-ups without a human or LLM polling
description:
Today the coordinator is the monitor. On 2026-09-15 every bridged stage needed a hand-written watch-*.py (Popen the driver, write a JSON heartbeat each minute from process state + run.jsonl mtime) plus a harness Monitor polling that heartbeat, re-armed every 30 minutes. That is LLM-and-human polling in the hot loop, the opposite of the LLM-in-the-loop principle (deterministic inner loop; judgment at seams).

Reference pattern: QM monitor poller (yc-software/qm e0b8686, src/monitors/monitor-poller.ts; comparison note in orchestrators/docs/research/agent-systems/comparison/qm-vs-workflow-interpreter.md). A durable monitor record stores a cursor and tail over a process output stream; a core poller (10 s) reads at most 64 KiB past the cursor and fires on new output, exit, TTL expiry, process loss, or a quiet heartbeat, with a minimum fire interval, max fires per tick, pattern filter, and idempotent fire keys; a fire enqueues a NEW turn rather than injecting into the live one. Borrow the pattern, not the code (their host is Postgres + Node; ours is bd + foreman tick).

Proposal for ours: (1) the foreman driver writes a heartbeat record (tick count, last event, current activation/gate, run.jsonl offset) on every tick; (2) a wake condition list on the instance: gate opened, root terminal, refusal written, driver exit, heartbeat stale > N; (3) when a condition fires, emit one durable wake event (bd event with an idempotent fire key = instance_key + condition + cursor) and run an optional host hook command (e.g. notify the coordinator session, or print a compact status) — never call a model; (4) a minimum fire interval and a per-instance cap so a flapping driver cannot spam; (5) compact status output that the coordinator reads instead of transcripts.

Out of scope: injecting into a running activation, any LLM call in the poller, multi-replica leader leases.
acceptance_criteria: Running phase-bridge on a stage and walking away yields exactly one durable wake event per gate opening, one on terminal, one on refusal, and one on stale heartbeat, each with an idempotent fire key; re-running the poller does not duplicate events; a host hook command receives the compact status; unit tests cover cursor advance, dedupe, min-fire-interval, and stale detection with a stub driver; no model is invoked anywhere in the path.

title: Record every collision as a decomposition signal against both stages

description:
Deferred from cr-xb2 round 4. Found by GPT-5.6 Sol, shape corrected by Opus 5; both verified independently.

supervisor/launch.py _reattach returns the durable receipt when receipt.state is STARTED and ledger.has_launch(receipt.launch_id), with NO comparison of which vendor the receipt describes, and dispatch then bypasses _launch. A pre-fix wrapper could launch the metadata-selected vendor, write receipt plus ledger line, and die before record_dispatch, leaving the activation MINTED. A post-fix wrapper then adopts that still-running foreign process, and supervisor/run.py observes its output through the root-selected profile.

Legacy-only: post-cr-xb2 no launch can write a receipt whose vendor differs from the root pin, because create_root freezes the resolution and _assert_same_instance makes it immutable per instance key.

SHAPE, corrected from Sols original proposal:
- No normalizer needed. Profile.name already returns the bare RunnerName value and _launch already holds profile. Store a plain str or None.
- Do NOT import profiles into supervisor -- profiles/registry.py imports supervisor.profile, so that direction is a cycle. Compare against the profile dispatch was handed.
- Follow the sandbox: SandboxMode = OFF precedent at supervisor/models.py:300 -- a defaulted flagging value whose only reachable source is a receipt from a launcher predating the field.
- CRITICAL: None means UNKNOWN, not foreign, and most such receipts describe the correct vendor. Mismatch (not None and != profile.name) should terminate/settle/halt. None should REFUSE TO ADOPT with a typed operator-readable refusal, ideally recording a deviation -- NOT kill. Sol proposed killing on None, which would destroy legitimate crash-window work on the first upgrade-straddling activation.
- Do not let the mismatch branch fall through to the existing ExecLedgerError path: it fails closed but blames an unexplained ledger line, and leaves the foreign child running with no max_wall and no exit record, which is the exact harm adoption exists to prevent.
- RECORD_MODEL is extra=forbid, so a new receipt read by an old binary parses as malformed; only matters on rollback.

RELATED, worth its own bead: the root pins a runner NAME, not an executable. ProfileConfig carries per-vendor binary overrides resolved from live config at profile_for time, so two wrappers under different config can exec different binaries for the same pinned name -- and a receipt field storing profile.name would see no mismatch.

title: Nothing asserts that implement's verify set must contain tests-untouched.sh
description:
Recorded as R4 Known gaps in docs/graph-loops/build-loop-tdd-enforcement.md, and measured rather than assumed.

Deleting the tests-untouched.sh entry from implement verify list leaves the graph VALID: load_graph returns no ERROR finding and the same single judgment_verify_superset warning. Two tests break and both do so incidentally -- the content-hash pin in tests/_helpers.py, and the drill at tests/test_build_loop_drills.py:333 which arms a failing tests-untouched.sh and asserts fail_code routes to implement, so it fails only because its armed script never runs.

Nothing asserts the rule itself.

This matters because R4 is the rule that dropped from tier 2 to tier 3. implement allowed_paths was widened from tests/unit/** to tests/** for cr-o85.34.21, so the mount no longer excludes tests/acceptance/ and this verifier is the entire remaining defense.

Cheap fix: a graph-level assertion in tests/test_build_loop_graph.py pinning implement verify set, with a comment naming cr-o85.34.21 and the tier migration. Then removing the verifier fails for the right reason instead of two wrong ones.

Filed from the disciplines review. Small and self-contained.

title: spike-then-harden is not expressible: no base-commit lineage primitive
description:
Found by Claude Fable 5.1 during the disciplines review; the largest of the gaps it named.

Spike-then-harden as a discipline means: explore freely in a spike, then harden by building on the PRE-SPIKE base with the spike diff as read-only knowledge. Its defining rule is lineage.

That rule cannot be stated today. intended_base_commit is a derived mint fact -- spec section 3.2 fixes it as the predecessor pre_attempt_commit on rework, else the instance branch head -- and mint facts are never caller-supplied. A forward edge from spike to harden therefore bases harden on the spike artifact, which is exactly what the discipline forbids.

Prose cannot substitute. An instruction saying "revert the spike first" cannot reset a base commit, and a reviewer cannot distinguish a genuine hand-revert from partial salvage of spike code.

What is needed is a pinned-body primitive, e.g. a per-node base = "predecessor_base". That is admissible under the mint-facts-are-derived rule, because the graph body is pinned data rather than a caller parameter -- the derivation stays fixed, the body selects which fixed derivation applies.

Until such a primitive exists, do NOT claim spike-then-harden via node instructions. It would be a discipline the system advertises and cannot enforce.

Blocked on the disciplines mechanism decision. Do not action standalone.
notes: Deferred 2026-09-21 with cr-o85.43: graph-language feature waiting on the disciplines ruling (out of v1, 2026-09-08).

title: No outcome in the closed enum can carry escalate-on-doubt
description:
Found during the disciplines review (Astra + Fable, independently).

Escalate-on-doubt as a discipline needs a node to emit a verdict meaning "I am not confident, route me elsewhere". The outcome enum is closed and has no such value, so any graph expressing it must overload an existing outcome -- in practice fail_plan.

That collides structurally: schema rule 4 permits exactly one edge per (from, outcome) pair. build-loop already routes implement --fail_plan--> triage_build. A doubt discipline wanting implement --fail_plan--> consult cannot coexist with it. Reviewers also already read fail_plan as "abandon this plan", so overloading it is semantically wrong as well as structurally blocked.

Adding a distinct outcome is a schema addition, not a migration: exclude_none emission leaves every existing graph byte-identical, so no pinned body or content hash moves.

Related and separate: escalate-AFTER-N-attempts is a different feature and is NOT expressible either, because on_exhausted must target a gate and gate_type is closed to human. ADR 0004 defers gate_type = model with a trigger. So the feasible form is escalate-when-the-node-says-so, i.e. the node holds the verdict, consistent with ADR 0004.

Blocked on the disciplines mechanism decision. Do not action standalone.
close_reason: Approved P5 implemented and verified: distinct doubt with real bound decision; full gates 1583 unit,143 proc,25 Beads,66 acceptance; Ruff/format/mypy clean; Fable high approved corrections/final deltas. Resumed live proof passed in360.11s with8 verified Claude/Codex activations, real overlap and combined landing bc3a1a80514970d702d20dd6d8013ec05b520c32. Fixture-only signatures. Evidence docs/workstreams/agent-bridge/verification/P5.md.

title: Legacy divergent activations settle on metadata runner while launching the pinned one
description:
cr-xb2 closed the launch half of runner divergence: run_wrapper now selects the profile from the root-resolved node. Settlement was deliberately left reading activation metadata (foreman/cases.py:320 and :341), which is correct in general -- replay must parse the output of the vendor that actually ran.

The residual: for an activation minted BEFORE the cr-xb2 mint guard whose stored runner_profile diverges from the root pin, the two halves now disagree. Dispatch launches the pinned vendor; settle replays with the metadata vendor, so attribution parses one vendor with anothers profile.

Scope is legacy data only. Every new mint stores root-derived runner and model (bdio/api.py), so divergence cannot be created going forward. Likely surfaces as a replay mismatch halt gate rather than silent corruption, but the EXIT_RECORDED branch has no prior evidence to compare against, so that is unverified.

Decide: migration/backfill for pre-guard activations, or a settlement-time consistency check that halts explicitly.
close_reason: Subsumed by cr-xb2 round 4 task 2 (commit 3ef12ba): foreman/cases.py:321 and :343 now derive the settlement profile from the root, so the launched and parsed vendors can no longer disagree.

title: re-verification stamps have no expiry, so a merge can silently invalidate them
description:
Process gap found 2026-09-08 during the post-cr-cwq bead review.

On 2026-09-07 a read-only audit re-verified ~22 deferred beads against commit ab84e58 and stamped each with: "RE-VERIFIED 2026-09-07 (gpt-5.6-terra high, read-only audit vs code at ab84e58): STILL-VALID. Evidence: <file:line>. Do not re-audit this against the code without new reason."

That stamp is good practice — it names the commit, cites evidence, and stops re-litigation. It has one hole: nothing detects when a NEW REASON has arrived.

Measured instance. The cr-cwq merge (912ef93) landed one commit after ab84e58 and invalidated two beads carrying that exact stamp, both dated the previous day: cr-o85.8 (TaskSpec has no effort field — cr-cwq added TaskSpec.effort at supervisor/profile.py:140) and cr-o85.13 (a per-vendor default model table belongs with the role map — superseded by cr-49v). A re-audit of the other 16 in the same family found all 16 still valid, so the stamp was right 16 times out of 18 — but the two failures were invisible until someone re-read them by hand.

The general shape: a stamp asserts a fact about code at a commit, and a later merge touching those files is precisely the new reason the stamp asks for, yet the stamp cannot know a merge happened.

## Scope sketch

Record the files a stamp depends on, not only the commit — the evidence citations already name them. Then a check can ask whether any of those paths changed since the stamped commit and flag the bead for re-verification. bd notes already carry the commit and the file:line, so the data is present and unparsed.

## Acceptance criteria

Given a bead whose re-verification note cites file:line evidence at a commit, a command reports whether any cited file has changed since that commit, and lists which beads need re-verification. Demonstrated against the real case: cr-o85.8 and cr-o85.13 flagged after 912ef93, the other 16 in that family not flagged.

title: harden create_root against incomplete role pins, and rule on the vendor-default sentinel
description:
Split out of cr-cwq on 2026-09-08 by an Opus 5 adjudication of a GPT-5.6 Sol finding. Two related leftovers, both deliberately deferred.

## 1. create_root does not validate role pins

bdio/roots.py:121 checks only "if not resolved_config" — non-empty. It never requires a usable model and effort per task role. Reproduced: a resolved_config pinning a real model on node.implement with NO effort key at all was accepted, and resolved_node then yielded effort=None.

cr-cwq closed this class at the argv boundary (adapters refuse rather than omit) and at resolved_node (role-scoped refusal), which together make the dispatch path safe. Validating at create_root would additionally stop a bad root from ever being persisted.

It was NOT made primary deliberately: it pushes task-role config semantics into the config-agnostic bdio layer and would triplicate the definition of "what is a task role". Belt-and-suspenders, wrong layer to lead with.

## 2. Policy ruling on MODEL_VENDOR_DEFAULT

The sentinel means "omit the model flag and let the CLI pick". After cr-cwq the reproducibility contract says a root pins exactly one model per role and either the CLI runs it or the activation fails. Those two statements are in tension.

The sentinel survives today only as a graph-authoring placeholder: both shipped graphs set model = "default" in their node bodies, and _resolved_config overwrites any graph-default model with the role binding real model before it reaches a TaskSpec. Every task node is role-bound by schema (graph_schema.json:185 admits a profile:<role> alias only), so no task node can reach dispatch still carrying the sentinel.

The ruling needed: does the sentinel keep any legitimacy for task roles, or is it retired — with the shipped graphs dropping their model = "default" lines, since the schema makes the field optional and the role binding supplies it regardless.

## Acceptance criteria

create_root refuses a resolved_config whose task role lacks a usable model or effort, with a test in both directions. The sentinel question is answered in an ADR or a comment at MODEL_VENDOR_DEFAULT, and the shipped graphs match the ruling.
close_reason: FIXED: bdio/roots.py:128-164 requires crew/model/effort per task node; 'default' refused at foreman/config.py:137, resolve.py:155, execution.py:141. Triage 2026-09-21 (Opus 5 medium, verified against code)

title: Record the served model set (result.modelUsage) on ActivationMetadata, not only in cost reports
description:
Split out of cr-cwq on 2026-09-08. Independent of fallback: it turns a pinned model from a CLAIM into a VERIFIED FACT.

cr-cwq pins model and effort per role into the immutable root. Nothing checks that the CLI honoured the pin. If a vendor silently substitutes, ignores an unknown alias, or routes to a different tier, the root still asserts the pinned model and no evidence contradicts it.

Measured by an Opus 5 review of the claude stream fixtures on 2026-09-08 — the served model is already present in the stream the profile parses, in three places:
- the system/init line carries "model" (tests/fixtures/profiles/claude/tools.jsonl:1, resume.jsonl:1)
- every assistant event carries message.model (tools.jsonl:3,4,8)
- the terminal result line carries modelUsage, an object keyed by every canonical model that actually consumed tokens, with per-model tokens and cost. The fixtures show TWO distinct models keyed in one run (result.json:1, live-result.jsonl:1), which is what makes this surface definitive rather than indicative.

modelUsage is the strongest surface: terminal, definitive, and it enumerates every served model by name.

## Scope

Thread a served-model field from the result event through RunnerEvent, LogScan and TerminalEnvelope (all three currently drop it) onto ActivationMetadata (bdio/wire.py:343-382, which today carries only the pinned model plus usage).

## Acceptance criteria

An activation whose CLI reports modelUsage records the served model set on its metadata; a mismatch between the pinned model and the served set is visible to a reader of the activation without re-reading logs. Decide deliberately whether a mismatch should also fail the activation and record the reasoning.

title: probe-driven model substitution ignores an overridden fallback_models chain
description:
Found by the Opus 5 critic on the cr-cwq round-1 diff, 2026-09-08.

foreman/resolve.py:439-451. NodeSetting.FALLBACK_MODELS was added to TASK_SETTING_TYPES (resolve.py:70-71), so the fallback chain is settable by project-config and instance-override. Claude honours such an override: its --fallback-model flows from the resolved setting through ResolvedNode.fallback_models into the TaskSpec. The codex/opencode probe does not — _available_model picks its substitute from binding.fallback, the raw TOML role binding, never from the resolved setting.

Failure scenario: an operator sets node.implement.fallback_models = "modelX" in project-config for a codex-bound role whose primary probe fails. The root records fallback_models = modelX, but the model actually pinned is the first available entry of the original TOML fallback list. The recorded chain and the used chain diverge silently, and the root is the artefact an auditor reads.

Deferred deliberately from cr-cwq: overriding a fallback chain was outside that bead brief, and the critic rated it narrow.

## Acceptance criteria

_available_model reads the resolved fallback chain rather than the raw binding, so an overridden chain drives the probe; a test sets fallback_models via project-config on a codex role with a failing primary probe and asserts the pinned model comes from the override.
close_reason: Superseded: owner decided 2026-09-08 to remove the fallback mechanism entirely rather than fix its override divergence. No fallback chain means nothing to override.

title: 26 open beads have no acceptance criteria (bd lint)
description: Cleanup residue found 2026-09-07. bd lint reports 26 open beads missing an Acceptance Criteria section: cr-7wi cr-b1p cr-bgp cr-e0a cr-n2z.5 cr-n2z.7 cr-o85.3 cr-o85.8 cr-o85.9 cr-o85.10 cr-o85.12 cr-o85.13 cr-o85.15 cr-o85.16 cr-o85.17 cr-o85.18 cr-o85.26 cr-o85.27 cr-o85.30 cr-o85.31 cr-o85.34 cr-o85.34.11 cr-o85.34.18 cr-o85.38 cr-t5x cr-ypz. Most now carry a 2026-09-07 re-verification note with file:line evidence instead, which is the more useful record.

title: feature-delivery test-protection check inspects only the last commit, not the whole attempt
description:
GPT-6 Astra audit 2026-09-07 via the phase-7 plan, which records the gap at docs/plans/workflow-interpreter-phase-7.md:216. scripts/review-checks.sh:27 checks the last commit only. A runner that touches protected test files in an earlier commit of a multi-commit attempt passes the check. The equivalent build-loop script tests-untouched.sh should be compared for the same shape.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. On a node whose verify set includes the test-protection check, have the runner make two commits.
2. In the first commit, modify a protected test file. In the second, touch only source.
3. Run the check: it inspects HEAD only, sees no test change, and passes.
acceptance_criteria: The check covers every commit from intended_base_commit to the artifact, not just HEAD; a test pins a two-commit attempt that touches tests in the first commit and is caught.

title: Codex review activations consume about 700k input tokens each
description: Fable 5.1 audit 2026-09-07 from the first live run baseline. The four codex reviewer activations in the 2026-09-05 build-loop run consumed 714k, 772k, 850k and 625k input tokens for 3.8k, 2.9k, 3.8k and 1.9k output — about 2.96M input tokens across one 73-minute run against a small slice. Reviewer briefs materialize whole diffs and whole output trees. This is the dominant per-run cost and nothing bounds it. Related to cr-o85.40 (no trimming exists) and cr-o85.34.18 (955 bd calls per run); distinct because it is about what the reviewer is SENT, not how it is assembled.
acceptance_criteria: Per-activation input tokens are measured across a second live run and compared to the first; the dominant contributor is named; a decision is recorded on whether to bound it.

title: design-spec graph needs a domain-specific (non-coding) verifier
description: Both audits 2026-09-07. workflows/feature-delivery.toml:5 and workflows/build-loop.toml:5 declare two CODING workflows. docs/ideas/workflow-graphs.md:27 proposed per-task-type graphs precisely so research and architecture work could get a different arc without editing skills, and :76 questions the abstraction value without genuinely different task types. Two coding loops do not test that hypothesis. A research graph has different artifacts (findings, sources, a written doc), different verification (citations resolve, claims are sourced) and different gates than an implement/review loop.
design: Pick one real research or architecture task from the backlog rather than inventing a fixture. The point is to discover which parts of the engine assume a diff-producing writer node. Expect the effects gate, artifact pinning and the verify contract to need work for a node whose output is prose.
acceptance_criteria: A non-coding graph runs one real task to a terminal; its verify scripts check something a coding graph cannot; the engine changes it forced are recorded.
notes: P5 delivered and ran the design/spec Markdown graph with actual Claude/Codex review and authenticated fixture landing. This older issue remains open because its additional domain-specific verifier criterion is not met by the shared verifier used in the six-phase proof. See docs/workstreams/agent-bridge/verification/P5.md.

title: Legacy uncoordinated roots: execution band keyed on wrapper_home, not repo
description:
GPT-6 Astra audit 2026-09-07, confirmed. foreman/config.py:42 builds wrapper_root from wrapper_home plus a hash of the repo path; owner.py:23 stores the ownership record inside that root; compose.py:160 creates the execution band from its paths. Spec section 4 says the band is one active runner ever for a repo, but the lock identity includes wrapper_home. Two configurations pointing different wrapper homes at the same checkout get two independent bands and can run two runners against one working tree. Spec section 14 documents this as a known siting deviation; no issue tracked resolving it.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Point one foreman config at wrapper_home A and a second at wrapper_home B, both over the same repo checkout.
2. Start an instance under each.
3. Both acquire a band and dispatch: the flock paths differ because they are derived under different wrapper roots, so neither excludes the other.
design: Blocking for concurrency work: leases and merge slots assume the band is authoritative per repo. Either derive the band path from the canonicalized repo identity alone, or refuse to start when another wrapper root already claims the repo.
acceptance_criteria: Two wrapper homes over one checkout cannot both hold the band; the second refuses with a message naming the holder; a test pins it.

title: Deferred phase-7 verify checks have prose triggers and no work items
description: GPT-6 Astra audit 2026-09-07. docs/plans/workflow-interpreter-phase-7.md D4 defers three checks: rows-vs-names.sh (no row-ID artifact convention exists), review-artifact.sh and claims-cited.sh (the reviewer findings go to a separate outputs ref and are absent from the checkout). Each defers on a condition stated only in plan prose, e.g. wait until a malformed findings file occurs. No issue carries those triggers, so nothing will ever surface them and they can stay deferred indefinitely.
design: Do NOT build the checks now; the deferral reasoning is sound. File the triggers so they are observable: what artifact convention would unblock rows-vs-names, and what observed failure would justify the other two.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the three deferred checks has a work item naming its observable trigger and the evidence that would justify building it; the phase-7 plan points at them instead of carrying the condition in prose.

title: Project brief and verification doc still say this repo has no first-party code
description: GPT-6 Astra audit 2026-09-07, confirmed. .claude/project/brief.md:6 says it is not an application; there is no first-party product code and no CI and :24 says no package to build or publish; no test/lint pipeline for the repo as a whole. .claude/project/verification.md:3 repeats it, then :51-53 defines the seven-gate Python pipeline over workflow_interpreter/. Both files are in the CLAUDE.md read order, so every fresh agent is told the engine does not exist before being shown its gate. This misdirects orientation on the single largest thing in the repo.
acceptance_criteria: brief.md and verification.md both describe workflow_interpreter/ as first-party code with a real gate; no sentence in either file denies its existence; the read order still points at them.
close_reason: brief.md + verification.md now describe workflow_interpreter/ as first-party code with a real gate (1e9ed7f).

title: build-loop red-test evidence is model-recorded, never mechanically checked
description:
GPT-6 Astra audit 2026-09-07, confirmed by reading the graph and script. workflows/build-loop.toml:38,49 instruct write_tests to produce tests that fail for the right reason, but its verifier scripts/checks/tests-parse.sh only COLLECTS tests; it never runs them against the absent implementation. review_tests adds assertion detection, not execution. So the red phase rests entirely on reviewer judgement.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. On the build-loop tests region, have write_tests emit a test file whose assertions already pass against the current tree (for example asserting something existing code already satisfies).
2. Run the node verify set: tests-parse.sh collects the tests and passes.
3. review_tests assertion-strength.sh finds assert statements and passes.
4. The tests region completes with no evidence any test ever failed.
design: Decide first whether observed red is REQUIRED evidence or advisory. If required, the check must distinguish an intended assertion failure from an import or setup error, otherwise a broken test file grades as a good red. That distinction is the hard part and the reason this was not built with the other four scripts.
acceptance_criteria: A tests-region node either produces recorded evidence that its tests ran and failed for an assertion reason, or the graph documents red as reviewer-judged and stops claiming it mechanically.

title: launch abort follow-ups: torn abort-pending receipt orphans the stub child; recover.py docstring lists two pre-checks not three; mint-block test uses a duck-typed stub
description: Critic minors on the cr-o85.35 fix round (accepted). (1) recover.py ~194-202: a TORN abort-pending receipt classifies as absent, so cases.route_head mint block passes and the infra retry mints while the un-ACKed stub child is still alive and now unowned (it never reached execvpe, so no second runner; one leaked stub process). Treat an unreadable receipt for a DISPATCH-less activation as abort-pending, or fail closed. (2) cases.py ~412-418: an unreadable /proc stalls the instance every tick with a bare stalled= string and no logged error, unlike _HALT_INDETERMINATE. (3) recover.py module docstring: three fail-closed pre-checks now, abort-pending first; the docstring is the ordering contract. (4) tests/test_foreman_cases.py ~110-136 proves the mint block with a duck-typed PendingAbortRecovery stub; add one case through the real Recovery.

Evidence: workflow_interpreter/supervisor/recover.py:194; workflow_interpreter/foreman/cases.py:413. An unreadable receipt becomes absent before the abort-pending check, so the fail-closed abort path is still bypassable. Do not re-audit this against the code without new reason; it was checked at this commit.

title: close.py fresh path records pre-existing deviations twice (finalize.decide already prepends them)
description: Critic on phase 3: foreman/close.py ~290 builds deviations = (*recorded.metadata.deviations, *decision.deviations) while finalize.decide returns (*activation.metadata.deviations, violation) — inherited from the pre-phase-3 decide (same tuple shape at aa08eb9). title: path_allowed vs plan_for grant mapping disagree on symlinked grant dirs and bare directory paths
description: Critic on phase 3 (cr-n2z.4): sandbox._grant_path realpaths the grant (mount source = target) while channels.path_allowed is lexical over the git repo-relative path. A grant link/** with link -> real/ mounts real/ rw; the runner writes link/x, git reports real/x, full_match(link/**) is False -> false EFFECT_OUTSIDE_ALLOWED_PATHS (and with the bound, a possible halt). Also path_allowed("src", ("src/**",)) is False for a path equal to the grant directory itself, which git reports for a dirty submodule or an untracked nested repo; mitigated today by -uall and workspace._assert_clean. Decide: refuse symlinked grant dirs at plan time (matches the .-segment refusal), and treat the bare grant directory as allowed. Latent edges, no live reproduction.

title: phase-5: foreman status surfaces only open HALT gates, never open TRANSITION gates — a waiting ship gate can be invisible
description: Found 2026-09-02 while adjudicating the round-2 6a disagreement. VERIFIED BY CODE READ: foreman/__main__.py:218-241 builds the status payload with root_id, activations, instance_base_commit, instance_branch_head, stale, and — only if frontier.open_halt is not None — open_halt. It never reports frontier.open_gates, which frontier.py:243 already computes and returns. Meanwhile foreman/tick.py:299 returns TickReport(terminal=...) on the fall-through path with NO opened_gate. CONSEQUENCE: a transition gate (e.g. the ship gate, GateReason.TRANSITION) is announced by exactly ONE TickReport.opened_gate, at the tick that opens it, and never again by any surface. A human who misses that single report — or whose foreman crashed in the 6a window before it was emitted (cr-hmm) — has no CLI signal that a gate is waiting for a signed decision. The instance is not stuck in any state the code considers wrong; it is simply invisible. NOT 6a-specific: the crash only guarantees the report is missed. This is the general case. SUGGESTED FIX: include frontier.open_gates in the status payload the same way open_halt is included, with the inbox path and payload template per gate. NOTE the interaction with cr-hmm: if status listed open transition gates, the delayed-backfill gap would be audit-only, which is what the round-2 brief provisionally assumed it already was.
acceptance_criteria: foreman status reports every open gate, not only halt gates, with enough detail for a human to submit a signed payload; a drill asserts a transition gate is discoverable on a tick AFTER the one that opened it.
notes:
REVERSED (2026-09-02, same session). The P1 escalation above was WRONG on two
counts, and the reversal is evidence-based.

1. There is NO notification requirement in the spec. The word "notification"
   occurs exactly ONCE in docs/specs/workflow-interpreter.md, at :863, and it
   is a WINDOW MARKER naming where the 6a crash lands — not a contract. The
   actual 6a requirement is the clause's own predicate: "re-tick converges, no
   duplicate gate (same key), no duplicate edge."
2. Spec:729 is explicit: **"Gates wait indefinitely in v1."** Waiting is the
   designed state, not a stall.

And the gate is NOT invisible. `bdio/gates.py:221-224` creates it as a durable
bd bead with a human-readable title (`_TITLE_GATE.format(gate_node, seq)`) and
logs `wf.gate.opened`. It is discoverable by `bd list --status=open` — the
issue tracker IS this system's durable store, and is exactly where a human is
expected to find waiting work. `foreman status` omitting open transition gates
is a UX nicety, which is what this bead is now scoped to.

Spec 6a is moreover ALREADY ASSERTED END TO END at
tests/test_foreman_e2e.py:292-359: converges (`opened_gate is None`, :314), no
duplicate gate (`len(lab.beads("gate")) == 1`, :340), no duplicate edge
(`events_backfilled == 2` then unchanged on re-tick, :356-359). The missed
event is backfilled exactly once at the next routing tick.

Sol's BLOCKER 1 does not survive the spec text. Fable's ruling stands. My own
"silent stall" escalation was an overclaim of the same species S1 exists to
catch, committed while adjudicating S1. Recorded here deliberately.

Re-scoped P1 -> P3, defect -> enhancement: make `foreman status` report
`frontier.open_gates` (frontier.py:243 already computes it) so a waiting
transition gate is visible without a `bd list`.
close_reason: FIXED. foreman/__main__.py status now reports open_gates — every OPEN gate, halt and transition alike — each with gate_id, node, reason, its inbox path and its unsigned payload template. open_halt kept unchanged for existing consumers. Test: tests/test_foreman_main.py::test_status_reports_an_open_transition_gate_with_its_inbox_and_template. Mutation-proven: filtering the new list back to HALT gates only (the exact pre-fix defect) turns the test RED. Motivation is operational, not the earlier 'silent stall' reasoning: status is the ONLY command that renders a gate inbox and payload template, and the shipped feature-delivery graph's ship and triage gates are both gate_type=human TRANSITION gates — so the live DRILL-27 acceptance (cr-o85.32) could not be driven by a human without this.

title: phase-5: a transition event missed by a 6a-window crash is NOT redelivered on re-tick — it waits for the next routing decision
description: Found by S1 batch 7 (2026-09-02) when injection point 6a was finally injected where the spec says: between gate persistence and its first notification. VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY: Foreman.tick() calls _backfill ONLY in the abandoned_halt branch (tick.py:272) and the head-routing branch (tick.py:277). Not in the dead_end branch, not in the empty/entry-mint branch, and not on the gate-intake path, which returns earlier. CONSEQUENCE: after a crash in the 6a window the gate bead has landed but its transition event has not, and the immediate re-tick backfills NOTHING (events_backfilled == 0) because the landed gate already consumes its source activation, so no routing decision remains to trigger the sweep. The event stays durably absent — never duplicated — until the next tick that takes ANY routing decision; in the drill that is the tick routing the closed ship gate to terminal, which then writes both outstanding events at once (events_backfilled == 2). An instance parked at an open gate awaiting a human keeps the event missing for that entire period. SPEC GAP: docs/specs/workflow-interpreter.md:861-863 says 'crash between gate-open and first notification ... => re-tick converges', which reads as immediate. It does not converge on re-tick. NOT yet classified as a correctness defect: events are a derived audit projection (bdio/bounds.py ceiling_count docstring excludes them) and nothing in routing reads them, so this looks like an audit-completeness and spec-wording gap rather than a control-flow bug. NEEDS A RULING: is delayed backfill the intended contract for anything downstream that watches transition events to know a transition occurred? The test now asserts the ACTUAL behaviour (0, 0, then 2) rather than the row's implied shape.
acceptance_criteria: Either the spec text is corrected to describe delayed backfill, or _backfill is called on the paths that currently skip it and the drill asserts immediate convergence.
notes:
SUPERSEDED IN SUBSTANCE by the cr-tl3 adjudication (round-2 sign-off).

This bead was filed as "6a leaves a transition event unbackfilled". That half is
NOT a defect: `_backfill` runs on the next edge-taking tick (tick.py:277), so
the event is reconstructed once the gate's payload is submitted. Spec §3.3:475
defines events as an idempotently reconstructible audit projection, which this
satisfies. The gap is audit latency bounded by the gate's lifetime.

The REAL defect the 6a analysis exposed is notification, not backfill, and it
lives on cr-tl3 (raised to P1). Close this one in favour of cr-tl3 unless the
latency itself is judged unacceptable.

Earlier correction retained: "nothing in routing reads events" is FALSE —
frontier.py:141-161 reads TERMINAL events for `terminal` and consumption.
close_reason: Not a defect. The 6a event gap is audit latency bounded by the gate's lifetime, and spec 3.3:475 defines events as an idempotently reconstructible audit projection. Already asserted end to end at tests/test_foreman_e2e.py:292-359, including the exactly-once backfill at the next routing tick. See cr-tl3 for the reversal record.

  continuation lifecycle: exit-recorded
  after continuation, worktree holds: ['scripts', 'src']
  reset_applied: True
  prereset refs: ['refs/wf/wf-1/prereset/wf-3']

Supervisor.run runs the same 5.4 precondition for a continuation as for any other activation. A continuation resuming a vendor session whose working tree has been reset under it is at least surprising.
